before.rationale: Jehoshaphat's prayer identifies the invading peoples as the neighbors Israel had spared and describes their assault on Israel's inheritance.

after.rationale: For Moab and Ammon, named in both passages, Jehoshaphat's prayer recalls Israel's earlier restraint and describes their assault on its inheritance; no identity between Minaeans and Mount Seir is asserted.

changes.reason: Narrowed the shared peoples to Moab and Ammon instead of potentially equating Minaeans with Mount Seir.

before.rationale: The command to stand and see the Lord's salvation without fighting directly recalls Israel's deliverance at the sea.

after.rationale: The promise that Judah will see the Lord's salvation without fighting recalls Moses' instruction to see God's salvation while the Lord fights.

changes.reason: Removed the word stand from the description of the Chronicles command because the supplied source says Understand these things.

before.rationale: Both describe the people's leaders escorting the king from the temple complex to the palace throne; the gate descriptions differ.

after.rationale: Both end the royal escort at the palace throne. Chronicles says the king was brought up into the Lord's house, while Kings says down from it; the gate descriptions also differ.

changes.reason: Made the differing directions in the preserved procession accounts explicit.

before.rationale: The preservation of Joash in Jehoiada's household and God's house is a concrete instance of the good for which the priest receives royal burial honors.

changes.reason: Removed attribution of the household rescue to Jehoiada personally; the separately retained covenant and temple restoration passage directly supports his good deeds.

before.rationale: The mighty force helping Uzziah describes the strength whose growth becomes the setting for his proud entry into the sanctuary.

changes.reason: Removed the general army-strength-to-pride link because it did not sufficiently illuminate the distinct troop number or military organization in this source unit.

before.rationale: The eighty priests' entry prepares their explicit opposition to the king's usurpation of Aaronic incense service.

after.rationale: The priests who follow Uzziah into the sanctuary act within the Aaronic responsibility to guard the holy things and altar against incursions that bring guilt and wrath.

changes.reason: Replaced a mere adjacent action-to-speech link with the specific legal responsibility explaining the priests intervention.
